newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid fuel prices hold with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid fuel prices hold with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices stayed little changed Tuesday despite the lack of utility demand, steadied by relatively low stocks and slight gains in crude, industry sources said.

"Short-term, there's still a lack of prompt supply, and if crude continues to hold, resid should too," said one cash trader, adding cheap gas and mild East Coast weather continued to trim utility demand.
In New York Harbor, prompt one percent was unchanged at $18.50-75 a barrel, with October paper also quoted steady at the same number. November paper was pegged at $18.75-19.00.
NYH high sulphurs also held relatively steady, with 2.2 percent still pegged at $17.00-17.25, traders said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, prices also were little changed, with one percent still at $16.75-17.00 and three percent at about $16.50.
Traders said 40,000 barrels of prompt USG three percent sold at $16.80 (FOB Houston).
Despite low burns and fuel switching to gas, some traders said they expected utilities to soon start stocking for winter.
